brief.headline: Aluminium fell for a third session, down $31.00 (-0.95%) to an official cash settlement of $3,248.00, after the supply headline that drove this week's seven-week high was retired: the world's largest alumina refinery outside China announced it is ramping back to full capacity three days after cutting to half rate, having secured regulatory approval to import its own gas. That is the third dated supply-relief fact in three sessions, and together they have taken $125.00 (-3.71%) out of the price - yet the physical evidence moved the other way again, with exchange inventory drawing for a 33rd consecutive day to below 250,000 tonnes and the front of the curve holding a premium for prompt metal for a second session running.
bullets: WHAT MOVED. LME official cash aluminium settled $3,248.00 on 14-August, down $31.00 (-0.95%) from $3,279.00, and the three-month settled $3,246.00, down $29.00 (-0.89%). That is a third consecutive fall. Measured from the 11-August high of $3,373.00 the give-back is $125.00 (-3.71%); measured from the 28-July swing low the market is still up $88.50 (+2.80%), so roughly two fifths of the August advance survives against three fifths yesterday. Unlike yesterday the base complex SPLIT - zinc +0.97% and copper +0.37% rose while aluminium, lead and nickel fell - which argues against a shared macro driver and points at something specific to aluminium. Note also that this run compiles on a Saturday: the 14-August board is the last published official until Monday's ring.

WHY IT MOVED, AND IT IS A SINGLE NAMED FACT. Norsk Hydro announced that Alunorte - a 6.3 million tonne a year refinery in Brazil, the largest alumina plant outside China - is ramping back up to full capacity, after Brazil's energy regulator approved it as a self-importer of natural gas and it struck a temporary terminal-access agreement with its gas supplier. The refinery had cut to half rate on 11-August on a gas shortage, and that disclosure was the catalyst that took the market to a seven-week high. Total lost production was 100,000 to 120,000 tonnes over three days. In other words, the strongest bullish supply fact of the week was created and retired inside the same week by the same company. It follows two other dated relief facts: a war-damaged Gulf smelter guiding back to pre-incident output in the first quarter of 2027, and a government package securing Australia's largest smelter with power contracted to 2038.

WHY THE PHYSICAL MARKET DISAGREED, AGAIN. Exchange inventory drew another 1,700 tonnes to 248,300 - a 33rd consecutive daily draw and the first print below 250,000 tonnes. And the cash-to-three-month spread stayed in backwardation, meaning buyers still paid more for metal today than for metal in three months. It narrowed from $4.00 to $2.00, but it SURVIVED a second session, which is the first two-day prompt premium since 04-August. The read-across from copper was emphatic: its prompt premium doubled in a single session to $411 a tonne, the widest of this cycle, on another stock draw. Seven weeks of continuous draws and firming prompt structure across the complex say the metal available right now is scarce; a three-day, $125 decline says the supply picture twelve months out is loosening. Both are true because they answer different questions.

WHAT TO WATCH. The most important level is now close: the market's last significant swing low sits at $3,229.50, just $18.50 below where cash settled, and it is the explicit line separating a continuing advance from a deeper correction. Beyond that, three things. First, whether the backwardation survives a third session when trading resumes on Monday - two days is a signal, three would be a trend. Second, the monthly carbon settlements for anodes, pitch and petroleum coke around the 17th-18th, into which crude has just rebounded 1.67% and European gas 1.70%, so cost risk points modestly upward. Third, Japanese quarterly premium negotiations conventionally open late this month against a settled third-quarter number of $395 a tonne - and the buyer's case strengthened materially this week with three dated supply-relief facts in three days.

lme.commentary: THE 14-AUGUST OFFICIAL PUT CASH AT $3,248.00 (-$31.00, -0.95%) AND THE 3-MONTH AT $3,246.00 (-$29.00, -0.89%), A THIRD CONSECUTIVE DECLINE TOTALLING $125.00 (-3.71%) FROM THE 11-AUGUST HIGH. Read the three sessions together and a clean sequence emerges. Monday-Tuesday the market made a seven-week high on an alumina outage. Wednesday and Thursday it gave back $94.00 on two dated supply-relief headlines out of the Gulf and Australia. Friday it gave back $31.00 more when the alumina outage itself was retired - Norsk Hydro announced Alunorte is ramping back to full capacity after Brazil's ANP approved it as a gas self-importer and a temporary terminal-access agreement was reached with CELBA. Three days, three supply-relief facts, and the last one cancelled the catalyst for the rally. WHAT DID NOT COOPERATE IS THE PHYSICAL EVIDENCE, AND IT IS THE REASON THIS IS NOT A SIMPLE BEARISH SESSION. Stock drew another 1,700 t to 248,300 t - a 33rd consecutive daily draw, a fresh cycle low and the first print below 250,000 t. The cash-3M spread stayed in BACKWARDATION for a second consecutive session at $2.00, narrowed from $4.00 but intact, and that is the first time the front end has held a prompt premium two days running since 04-August. Seven weeks of continuous draws and a two-day backwardation say the prompt market is tight; a three-day, $125.00 decline says the forward supply story is loosening. Both are true, and they are answering different questions. THE COMPLEX SPLIT, WHICH SHARPENS THE READ. Zinc +0.97% and copper +0.37% rose while aluminium, lead and nickel fell, against all five falling together yesterday. A split complex points away from a shared macro driver and toward the metal-specific headline - and the dollar eased 0.33%, so the macro backdrop was marginally supportive rather than obstructive. Copper's own front end told the tightness story in the extreme: its cash settled $14,545.00 against a 3-month of $14,134.00, a $411.00 backwardation widened from $203.00 in one session, on a 2,750 t stock draw.

THE TARIFF ARITHMETIC MOVED EVEN THOUGH THE ASSESSMENT DID NOT, AND THIS IS THE ONE US NUMBER THAT REFRESHES EVERY SESSION. Against the carried $2,380/t transaction level the tariff accounts for roughly 68% of the total. Two thirds of a US delivered premium is policy arithmetic that changes with the LME price, not a measure of American physical tightness, and any US-facing analysis that treats the whole number as a market signal is reading the tax as though it were the market.

The domestic supply pipeline continues to build against it: Century's Mt. Holly has been at full capacity since 27-July for the first time since 2015 and Magnitude 7 Metals targets a partial New Madrid restart before year-end. More domestic metal behind a 50% tariff wall is the mechanism by which a US premium eventually falls without the tariff changing at all.

prices.label: Alumina FOB East Australia (SMM reported trade)
prices.note: HELD AT $356/mt FOB EAST AUSTRALIA (SMM-reported transaction of 30,000 mt for September loading dealt 05-Aug-2026, published 06-Aug). NO PUBLIC SEABORNE ALUMINA PRICE PRINT DATED AFTER THE ALUNORTE EVENTS HAS BEEN FOUND AT THIS COMPILE, SO NO VALUE ON THIS PANEL IS CHANGED FOR A FOURTH RUN - the events are recorded, the price is not invented. THE SUPPLY EVENT RESOLVED, AND IT RESOLVED FAST. Norsk Hydro announced that Alunorte in Barcarena, Para - 6.3 Mt/y nameplate and the largest alumina refinery outside China - is RAMPING BACK UP TO FULL CAPACITY after Brazil's regulator ANP approved the refinery as a self-importer of natural gas and a temporary terminal-access agreement was reached with gas supplier CELBA. The disruption ran three days from the 11-August disclosure of a cut to 50% of capacity. Lost production is put at 100,000-120,000 tonnes and the guided potential Q3-2026 Bauxite & Alumina impact of US$75-100 million is unchanged, reflecting both the lost tonnes and gas purchased above contract price. WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THIS PANEL, STATED HONESTLY: the outage never lasted long enough to produce a public seaborne price print, so the cost consequence was never observed on this board and now probably never will be. Roughly 3 Mt/y of annualised alumina was off the balance for three days - about 50-60 kt on a pro-rata basis, which reconciles broadly with the company's own 100-120 kt figure covering the full reduced-rate period. That is a rounding error against a 145 Mt/y global market. The correct read is that the alumina threat to smelter margin has been withdrawn, not that it was priced and passed. THE OTHER RECENT PRINT, STATED SEPARATELY BECAUSE THE BASIS DIFFERS AND MUST NOT BE BLENDED: SMM published on 11-August that 30,000 mt traded at $365/mt CIF MALAYSIA for September shipment, dealt 07-Aug-2026. CIF Malaysia is a delivered price including freight; FOB East Australia is a load-port price, so the $9/mt gap is broadly freight rather than a $9/mt rally. MARGIN CONTEXT AT TODAY'S LOWER METAL PRICE, AND THE RATIO MOVED AGAINST SMELTERS FOR A THIRD SESSION: against the 14-August three-month official of $3,246.00 the FOB mark now sits at about 11.0% of the metal price and the CIF mark at about 11.2%, up from 10.9% and 11.1% yesterday purely because metal fell again. Both remain well below the decade rule of thumb of roughly 15-17%, so the alumina leg is still a TAILWIND to smelter economics - and with Alunorte restored, the most credible threat to that tailwind this year has been removed inside a week.

Those are annual realisations on a different basis from a spot index and must not be blended into this row, but they independently place the market in the mid-$350s to low-$360s and confirm how far alumina has fallen year-on-year.

prices.label: SMM Alumina Index (China)
prices.note: SMM Alumina Index (China domestic). Carried at its stated date - no fresher public print was returned this run. THE MOST USEFUL RECENT CHINESE ALUMINA DATAPOINT REMAINS A COST NUMBER, NOT A PRICE: SMM published on 11-August that China's national weighted-average FULL production cost for alumina was RMB 2,718/mt in July, UP RMB 37/mt month-on-month, with the weighted-average CASH cost at RMB 2,544/mt. SMM guides August full cost to RMB 2,700-2,820/mt and cash cost to RMB 2,530-2,650/mt. The rise is attributed almost entirely to bauxite - higher imported CIF costs on elevated ocean freight plus the Guinea rainy season, and persistently tight domestic ore after mining-accident after-effects slowed restarts - partly offset by a small decline in energy costs. NOTE THE ASYMMETRY THIS CREATES WITH THE ALUNORTE EVENT: China's alumina cost floor is rising for domestic reasons at the same time as roughly 3 Mt/y of non-Chinese seaborne supply sits at half rate. The two are independent and they push the same way.

prices.label: Bauxite (SMM imported index / Guinea CIF China)
prices.note: Carried at the 06-Aug-2026 SMM Bauxite Weekly Review. THE NEXT EDITION IS DUE TODAY on the publication's Thursday cadence and had not printed at this 03:40 London compile, so the row is carried rather than marked. SMM Imported Bauxite Index $71.57/mt, UP $0.70 week-on-week, Guinea CIF $70-74/mt (average +$1 w/w), Guinea FOB $38-42/mt (average +$1 w/w). CORROBORATION FROM THE 11-AUGUST COST REVIEW: imported bauxite prices 'sustained their upward trend in July, serving as the core driver behind the cost surge', citing elevated ocean freight and the Guinea rainy season reducing shipments, plus slow domestic Chinese mine resumption - to the point that 'some alumina producers have been forced to adjust production schedules'. SMM's forward view: 'no clear timeline has emerged for domestic supply recovery, while imported ore shipments are expected to shrink further amid the rainy season. Bauxite prices are likely to hold high and steady, with import quotes potentially edging slightly higher.' STRUCTURAL DEVELOPMENT CARRIED FROM LAST RUN: Guinea's Mines Minister Bouna Sylla said state-owned Nimba Mining will sell bauxite to global traders and miners through MONTHLY TENDERS, with minimum guaranteed annual volumes under partner agreements and additional output sold via monthly spot tenders; CEO Patrice L'Huillier named Mercuria, Glencore, Rio Tinto and Vedanta as potential partners. Monthly tendering adds genuine public price discovery to the world's most important seaborne bauxite source and simultaneously shifts volume from contract to spot, which raises price variance in an already tight rainy-season market. THE NEXT SCHEDULED HARD DATAPOINT REMAINS THE GUINEA AUGUST LONG-TERM CONTRACT, still under negotiation against July's settlement of $70-71.5/mt. DRIVER DOWN, UNCHANGED: Chinese refinery bauxite inventories at roughly 94 days of cover. This remains the best-evidenced upward-trending input on the whole board.

prices.label: Caustic soda (China alumina-plant contract, Shanxi)
prices.note: CNY 2,090/t delivered, 50% ion-membrane liquid on a 100% NaOH basis - the JULY purchase price at Shanxi alumina plants, held flat month-on-month. THE VALUE IS DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED because August contracts have not settled and no new public mark was returned this run. GUIDANCE CARRIED AND IT IS WHY THE TREND FLAG IS UP: SMM's alumina cost review states that Shanxi caustic soda long-term contract prices are EXPECTED TO RISE BY RMB 50/mt in August, while Guangxi prices are set to DECLINE FURTHER BY RMB 150/mt. That is an explicit regional divergence, not a national move: the north tightens slightly, the south loosens and widens its cost advantage. SMM's assessment of the aggregate effect is that caustic 'had limited impact on alumina production costs' in July and will show 'overall narrow fluctuations' in August. AN EXPECTATION IS NOT A SETTLEMENT: the RMB 50/mt is carried as guidance in this note only and has not been written into the value, which stays at the last settled July figure.

prices.note: China average quicklime for alumina refining, carried at its stated date - no newer public assessment was returned this run and this row has no weekly public series, so gaps stay gaps. Lime is a small share of refinery cash cost and is not a swing factor in the current cost picture; SMM's 11-August cost decomposition attributes July's RMB 37/mt rise to bauxite, with caustic regionally divergent and energy slightly lower, and does not identify lime as a driver.

notes: ALUNORTE IS BACK - THE DEFINING ALUMINA FACT OF THE WEEK REVERSED IN THREE DAYS. Norsk Hydro disclosed on 11-August that Alunorte had cut to 50% of capacity after gas supplier CELBA notified disruptions to natural gas availability, and announced on 13-August (carried widely 14-August) that production is ramping back to FULL capacity following ANP approval to self-import gas and a temporary terminal-access agreement with CELBA. Lost production 100,000-120,000 t; guided potential Q3-2026 Bauxite & Alumina impact US$75-100m, unchanged. THE LESSON FOR THIS DASHBOARD IS ABOUT DURATION RATHER THAN MAGNITUDE: a headline capable of driving the LME to a seven-week high was fully retired before a single public seaborne alumina price print could register it. Supply events on this board are being priced faster than they are being measured.

headlines.title: ALUNORTE RAMPS BACK TO FULL CAPACITY AFTER THREE DAYS - THE CATALYST FOR THE WEEK'S HIGH IS RETIRED. Norsk Hydro announced that the Alunorte refinery in Barcarena, Para - 6.3 Mt/y nameplate and the largest alumina plant outside China - is ramping production back to full capacity, after Brazil's oil, natural gas and biofuels regulator ANP approved the refinery as a self-importer of natural gas and it reached a temporary terminal-access agreement with gas supplier CELBA. Alunorte had cut to 50% of capacity on 11-August when CELBA notified disruptions to gas availability, a disclosure that helped drive the LME to a seven-week high. Lost production over the reduced-rate period is estimated at 100,000-120,000 tonnes. The guided potential Q3-2026 Bauxite & Alumina financial impact of US$75-100 million is unchanged, covering both the lost tonnes and gas purchased above contract price.

A THIRD DOWN SESSION. The 14-August LME official put cash at $3,248.00, down $31.00 (-0.95%), and the 3-month at $3,246.00, down $29.00 (-0.89%). Because this run compiles on a Saturday, the 14-August board is the final published official until the 17-August ring - there is no pending print today.

This is the specific test set by yesterday's read: through the first half of August the front end repeatedly flickered into a prompt premium and surrendered it the next day, and two consecutive days is a materially different signal. Spread and flat price moved together this session, so the opposite-direction divergence that defined mid-week has closed - by price falling to the curve, not by the curve giving way. Proportion: $2.00 is 0.06% of cash.

A 33RD CONSECUTIVE DRAW TAKES STOCK BELOW 250,000 t FOR THE FIRST TIME THIS CYCLE. LME aluminium warehouse stock fell 1,700 t to 248,300 t on 14-August. That is seven weeks of uninterrupted daily draws, sustained through a three-session $125.00 price decline - precisely the conditions under which a financially-motivated draw would be expected to pause. Stock has fallen from 416,775 t at end-March and 264,400 t at end-July. It is the strongest public evidence for physical tightness available on this board.

COPPER'S BACKWARDATION DOUBLED IN ONE SESSION TO $411 - THE CONTROL EXPERIMENT FOR ALUMINIUM'S DECLINE. Copper cash settled $14,545.00 against a 3-month of $14,134.00, widening the prompt premium from $203.00 to $411.00, the widest recorded on this dashboard. Cash rose $260.00 (+1.82%) while the 3-month rose $52.00, so essentially the whole move was at the prompt date, and it came with a 2,750 t stock draw to 204,975 t - down from 249,850 t at end-July, an 18% reduction in ten sessions. THE COMPLEX SPLIT FOR THE FIRST TIME THIS WEEK, WHICH SHARPENS THE ATTRIBUTION. On 3-month officials zinc rose 0.97% and copper 0.37%, while aluminium fell 0.89%, lead 0.63% and nickel 0.39%. Yesterday all five fell together, which pointed at a shared macro or positioning factor. Today's split points the other way: when metals diverge, metal-specific explanations become the better ones - and aluminium had a dated, metal-specific supply headline while copper and zinc had collapsing warrant stocks.

THE DOLLAR EASED 0.33% AND ALUMINIUM FELL ANYWAY - WHICH REMOVES THE LAST ALTERNATIVE EXPLANATION. The US dollar index marked 99.636, its largest daily fall of the week, with the euro up 0.36% at 1.15694 and the yen firmer at 159.326. A weaker dollar mechanically cheapens dollar-denominated metal for non-dollar buyers and normally lifts the complex; two of five base metals did rise. Aluminium declined into a supportive currency backdrop on a session with a dated supply headline. The attribution is not ambiguous.

ENERGY REBOUNDED HARD INTO THE CARBON SETTLEMENT WINDOW. Brent rose 1.67% to $88.520 and European gas TTF rose 1.70% to EUR 61.43/MWh - the largest single-session energy moves of the week, reversing two soft sessions. Both feed smelter cost. TTF is the marginal power input for the European fleet, so a rising gas price alongside a falling metal price is a double-sided margin compression for EU smelters. Crude is the feedstock chain behind green petroleum coke and therefore behind calcined coke, pitch and the prebaked anode settlement due around the 17th-18th, so it firms the directional risk into that window.

INDIAN ALUMINIUM PRODUCER SHARES REPORTED LOWER ON THE ALUNORTE RECOVERY. The reasoning is the mirror image of the integrated-producer trade: a restored 6.3 Mt/y refinery removes the upside risk to seaborne alumina prices that had been supporting the realisations of producers with surplus alumina to sell. It is a useful reminder that alumina supply events cut in opposite directions across the value chain - a headline that compresses a merchant smelter's cost is the same headline that compresses an integrated producer's alumina revenue.

Read together they say the metal made its low around the official and stabilised into the afternoon, which is more informative than either number alone and is the sort of divergence that gets misreported as a data error.

backtest.verdict: These condition indicators showed NO predictive edge when tested: a 38.4% directional hit rate against a 71.2% naive 'always higher' baseline over the same sample, and forward returns after 'tightening' readings averaged 1.74% versus 7.04% after 'loosening' readings. They are therefore published as a read on CURRENT market condition only — not as a price forecast. The forward baseline and probability range above are the forward-looking view.
backtest.caveat: Measured on overlapping 13-week windows of weekly LME data (99 observations, 2024-05-24 to 2026-05-15). Overlapping windows overstate significance and the sample spans a single, largely rising market — evidence in either direction is weak.

earnings.note: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

catalysts.text: THE 17-AUGUST LME OFFICIAL - THE FIRST NEW RING SINCE FRIDAY AND THE TEST IS SPECIFIC ON TWO LEVELS. FIRST, THE WAVE (iv) LOW AT $3,229.50, now just $18.50 below the cash settlement of $3,248.00. It is the single explicit invalidation on the short-term Elliott count: holding it keeps the impulse-continuation count alive, a decisive close beneath it promotes the bearish alternate and opens $3,205 (wave i) and then $3,159.50 (wave ii). SECOND, WHETHER THE BACKWARDATION SURVIVES A THIRD SESSION. Two consecutive days is the first two-day prompt premium since 04-August and is a signal; three would make it a trend and would be the strongest evidence this cycle that the physical market is tightening independently of financial positioning. A slip back into contango marks the two-day premium as noise. Watch the stock line alongside: a 34th consecutive draw would extend the divergence, and any interruption removes the bull case's best evidence. Note there is no ring over the weekend, so the 14-August board stands until Monday.

MONTHLY CARBON SETTLEMENT WINDOW - prebaked anodes, coal tar pitch and green petroleum coke settle around the 17th-18th. This is the next scheduled opportunity to append sourced marks to the input-basket histories for those rows, all of which are currently carried at their June or July cycles and were NOT estimated this run. THE DIRECTIONAL RISK INTO THE WINDOW TURNED MODESTLY UPWARD AGAIN: Brent rebounded 1.67% to $88.52 on 14-August after two soft sessions, and green coke is a refinery by-product whose price follows crude with a lag. A firmer crude complex into a settlement window argues for carbon costs holding or edging up rather than falling.

MJP Q4-2026 PREMIUM NEGOTIATIONS conventionally open against the Q3-2026 settlement of $395/t CIF Japan. Nothing dated after the 06-July settlement has published. THE BUYER'S CASE STRENGTHENED MATERIALLY THIS WEEK AND THAT IS WHY THE SCENARIO RANGE IS NARROWED TO $310-405 WITH THE CEILING CUT MORE THAN THE FLOOR. Buyers now hold three dated public supply-relief facts from three consecutive sessions - the Gulf smelter's Q1-2027 recovery path, the Tomago power settlement to 2038, and the Alunorte return to full rate - plus the CIF Japan spot reference sitting $25/t BELOW the settled quarterly number. Sellers retain 33 consecutive stock draws to a fresh cycle low below 250,000 t and a front end that has held a backwardation two sessions running. For reference, Q3 opening offers ran $440-480/t and settled at $395/t.

THE PERMANENCE OF THE ALUNORTE GAS ARRANGEMENT. Norsk Hydro's own language is that the terminal-access agreement with CELBA is TEMPORARY, alongside ANP approval for the refinery to act as a self-importer of natural gas. The outage is resolved on a run-rate basis but the underlying gas supply arrangement is not permanently settled, and a 6.3 Mt/y refinery is large enough that any recurrence is material to the seaborne alumina balance. The thing to watch is a further company disclosure converting the temporary arrangement into a durable one - or failing to.

THE FIRST PUBLIC SEABORNE ALUMINA PRINT AFTER THE FULL ALUNORTE EPISODE. No public transaction print dated after 07-August has been found, so the entire three-day outage and its resolution passed without registering on any alumina price series available here. The next print is what confirms whether the episode left any mark at all on the seaborne market. The prior expectation, stated so it can be checked, is that it did not: 100-120 kt of lost production against a roughly 145 Mt/y global market is inside the noise.

SMM BAUXITE WEEKLY REVIEW. The last edition carried here (06-August) had the SMM Imported Bauxite Index at $71.57/mt, up $0.70 week-on-week, with Guinea CIF at $70-74/mt. Bauxite is the identified core driver of the rise in Chinese alumina full production cost and remains the best-evidenced upward-trending input on this board - the structural cost pressure that survives the Alunorte resolution entirely, because it is about ore supply and freight rather than about one refinery's gas contract. The August Guinea long-term contract remains under negotiation against July's $70-71.5/mt settlement.

risks.text: SUPPLY RELIEF ARRIVES ON A DATED, PUBLISHED SCHEDULE AND CAPS THE RECOVERY - THE RISK THAT MATERIALISED THIS WEEK AND THE REASON THE PRICE FELL THREE DAYS RUNNING. For months the returning capacity on this board was a list of intentions. In three sessions three of them acquired dates and numbers: EGA's H1 release on 12-August put Al Taweelah at about 18% of capacity with pre-incident hot metal guided for Q1-2027 and roughly US$400m allocated; on 13-August Tomago, up to 590,000 t/y, was secured by a A$2.5bn support package with power contracted to 2038; and on 13/14-August Alunorte returned to full rate after a three-day outage. Add Slovalco's 75,000 t/y in Q4-2026, Magnitude 7 Metals' 75,000 t/y at New Madrid before year-end, Mt. Holly already at full capacity, and SMM's outside-China daily average output already +1.6% month-on-month in July. TREND UP, HIGH IMPACT: this is no longer a forecast, it is a published schedule, and the market has taken $125.00 out of the price in three sessions on the first three entries in it.

THE STOCK DRAW STOPS OR REVERSES AND REMOVES THE BULL CASE'S BEST EVIDENCE. Seven weeks of consecutive draws are the single strongest public argument for tightness on this board, and the argument dies the day metal starts returning to warrant. TREND DOWN: today provided evidence AGAINST this risk for a third consecutive session - the draw continued for a 33rd session to 248,300 t, the first print below 250,000 t, and it did so on a third down day, precisely when a financially-motivated draw would be expected to pause. The complex corroborated: copper drew 2,750 t, zinc 4,550 t and lead 1,700 t on the same session. The honest caveat is unchanged - the draw cannot continue indefinitely and the lower stock goes, the more consequential any single delivery-in becomes.

PROLONGED HORMUZ CLOSURE KEEPS GULF SUPPLY IMPAIRED - AND THIS WEEK DEMONSTRATED HOW SENSITIVE THE MARKET IS TO ANY CHANGE IN THAT ASSUMPTION. Day 167 since the 28-February shutdown, with no development reported since Iran's state broadcaster restated on 11-August that the Strait remains closed until conditions are met. The Gulf was around a tenth of global primary production pre-conflict. TREND FLAT: nothing changed in substance this run. Note the free calibration the week provided - repricing three individual assets moved the market 3.7% in three sessions, so a change in the Strait regime itself would be an order of magnitude larger, in either direction. Note also the disagreement between the two Gulf-risk proxies today: crude rose 1.67% while aluminium fell 0.95%.

CHINESE PHYSICAL DEMAND WEAKENS AT THIS PRICE LEVEL. SMM's recent South China reviews have had holders lowering offers into discounts, downstream buyers standing aside on expectations of lower prices, traders pushing for discounted cargoes, and ADC12 secondary alloy quotes cut on falling metal and scrap costs. China is roughly 60% of global output and the marginal consumer of most seaborne units. TREND UP: buyer resistance has now been reported on both the way up and the way down, which is the more concerning version - it says the resistance is to the level, not to the rate of change. No new SMM spot review dated after 14-August has published at this Saturday compile, so this is carried on the most recent evidence rather than re-marked.

POSITIONING UNWIND IN A CROWDED LONG. This desk argued for a week that a rally making new highs while the front end surrendered its premium was carried by expectation rather than prompt need. $125.00 has now come out of the price in three sessions. TREND DOWN, AND FOR THE SAME SECOND REASON AS YESTERDAY: the front end held a backwardation THROUGH the decline, for two consecutive sessions. Length leaving a market normally loosens the prompt date; here it tightened and then stayed tight. The residual exposure is materially lower than it was at $3,374.00 and the liquidation has not damaged the prompt structure.

AN ALUMINA COST SHOCK RE-EMERGES. TREND DOWN, AND THIS IS THE CLEAREST DE-RISKING ON THE BOARD THIS RUN. The Alunorte gas disruption - the only credible alumina cost threat of the year - resolved in three days: Norsk Hydro announced a ramp back to full capacity after ANP approved self-import of natural gas and a temporary CELBA terminal-access agreement was reached. Lost production was 100,000-120,000 t, a rounding error against a roughly 145 Mt/y global market, and the outage never lasted long enough to register in a public seaborne price print. The carried FOB East Australia mark of $356/mt is about 11.0% of the 14-August three-month price against a decade rule of thumb of 15-17%, so alumina remains a clear tailwind to smelter margin. The residual risk is that the CELBA agreement is explicitly TEMPORARY, so the gas arrangement is not permanently settled.

SMELTER ENERGY AND CARBON COSTS RE-INFLATE INTO THE MONTHLY SETTLEMENT WINDOW. TREND UP, AND THIS IS THE ONE COST LINE THAT TURNED AGAINST SMELTERS THIS SESSION. Brent rose 1.67% to $88.52 and European gas TTF rose 1.70% to EUR 61.43/MWh, the largest single-session energy moves of the week, reversing two soft sessions. TTF is the marginal power input for the European fleet, so rising gas alongside a falling metal price is a double-sided margin compression for EU smelters and makes the Slovalco restart economics more fragile than the headline metal price implies. Crude feeds green petroleum coke and therefore calcined coke, pitch and the prebaked anode settlement due around the 17th-18th, so the directional risk into that window is modestly upward.

balance.label: Deficit - Goldman -720 kt, Norsk Hydro -900 kt, Macquarie -930 kt; Citi an outlier at -2.7 Mt. China alone ran a 322 kt deficit in June, and exchange inventory at a fresh century low leaves no absorption capacity

Consensus expects surpluses as Gulf output recovers and Indonesia ramps; Concord Resources warns the market may be 'too complacent about supply risks' in the meantime. Rio Tinto's 40% Yarwun alumina cut from October 2026 trims one input to that surplus REVIEWED 13-AUG: no balance-relevant datapoint changed on 12-August. Exchange inventory drew for a 31st consecutive session, 1,700 t to 251,700 t, and the draw rate ACCELERATED from the 1,500 t/day that had run for six of the seven prior sessions - the tightening in visible metal continued on a day the price fell 1.94%. Against that, Alunorte remains at 50 percent with roughly 3 Mt/y of seaborne alumina out, which is an upstream cost event rather than a metal balance event and should not be double-counted as a supply deficit for primary aluminium.
